archetypes.name: scope-flow
archetypes.rationale: The diff threads a new staged scope anchor through many plan-review surfaces where dropped keys or stale feature context would defeat the fix.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace SCOPE_ANCHOR_FILE from materialization through scout, panel, voters, revise, result env handoff, and MainAgent fallback. Look for any path where brainstorm-expanded context or IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR can still become the binding anchor, or where early exits fail to preserve the sanitized staged path. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: marker-flow
archetypes.rationale: The new [SCOPE-REDUCTION] marker has a complex lifecycle across detector, dedup, aggregation, voting, and renumbering.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the leading [SCOPE-REDUCTION] marker lifecycle across detection, collect-style severity prefixes, plan-review dedup, aggregation, ballot renumbering, and tally behavior. Check for marker loss, false positives, helper failure handling, tagged OOS special-case leaks, or duplicate heading regressions. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: prompt-sandbox
archetypes.rationale: The change inlines untrusted issue text into external-reviewer and voter prompts, making prompt-injection framing and escaping high risk.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review every place scope-anchor contents are embedded into prompts or durable handoff state. Focus on redaction, tag escaping, closing-tag injection resistance, path validation, and consistency of untrusted-data framing between reviewers, voters, revise, and fallback adjudication. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: bash-portability
archetypes.rationale: The diff adds substantial Bash plus embedded Python in runtime scripts where quoting, set -e, temp files, and Bash 3.2 compatibility can regress production flows.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the new and modified shell scripts for quoting mistakes, unsafe command substitutions, set -e surprises, tempfile cleanup gaps, Bash 3.2 portability issues, and Python subprocess assumptions. Pay special attention to helper invocation paths, mktemp locations, arrays, and fallbacks after failed validation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: compat-mode
archetypes.rationale: Several shared scripts gain optional plan-review behavior that must not alter existing code-review or default prompt contracts.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that optional scope-anchor behavior is isolated to plan-review callers and preserves default outputs for shared voter, tally, aggregation, and summary/report surfaces. Look for unintended code-mode behavior changes, byte-compatibility breaks when flags are omitted, or inconsistent documentation of shared-script contracts. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
